finding: External dispose closes lifecycle while an admitted root drains. Legacy operation() rejects a later write as disposed before poisoning. A swallowed rejection would let a readonly root report success, contrary to the explicit poison contract.
decision: Tag only new readonly roots. A direct write attempted after disposal still poisons that admitted readonly root before rejecting. A newly invoked canonical transaction after disposal also invalidates readonly-root success, because its read/write callback is no longer admissible; that callback is not executed.
preserved: Existing mutable-root behavior and all original transactions remain semantically unchanged. An admitted readonly root with no new post-dispose admission can drain. Closed/captured roots cannot borrow a later generation.
qualification: Deterministic barriers: root admitted, external dispose starts, write/transaction attempts caught, root rejects and dispose drains; no persistent effect. No timing sleeps.
source: cold_review59 static counterexample; root accepted before edits
